edits.current:
C/C++ execute closure inputs, Lean-produced results and arguments sent to host callbacks for `Fin` and selected `Subtype` values, including supported copied containers and mixed refined and unrefined arguments. The [hosted synchronous callback Subtype matrix](../evidence/callback-subtype-promotion-20261022.md) extends the two selected-Subtype directions to all sixteen non-PHP-Wasm consumer profiles on ordinary-source and reviewed-IR packages. A selected Subtype produced by Lean crosses a host callback argument or returned-closure result as its proof-erased base value. A base value produced by the host is checked by the selected Lean constructor when it is returned from a callback or passed into a returned Lean closure. For a host callback result containing a selected Subtype, the host supplies one typed recovery value before the call: the C callback descriptor's `recovery` pointer, the generated `with_recovery(callback, value)` API in C++, Python, Ruby and Rust, `Runtime::Callback` in CPAN, or the corresponding generated typed wrapper in the other installed profiles. The public wrapper validates and copies recovery before Lean or the callback runs. Recovery exists only for Lean's failure path and is never successful output. Missing or invalid recovery prevents callback entry; rejection preserves caller values, and a later valid call succeeds. The separate C/C++ `Fin` host-reply checks record first-error preservation and suppression of later callbacks. [PHP-Wasm callback Subtypes](../evidence/callback-subtype-php-wasm-local-qualification-20261022.md) have a separate local Node/Chromium qualification on both source routes. Nested callbacks, retained or asynchronous callbacks, arbitrary predicates, owned callback Subtypes, recursive or generic refined payloads, dispatch cost and peak memory remain separate work. The [hosted callback checked-record matrix](../evidence/callback-checked-record-promotion-20261023.md) separately establishes synchronous proof-free checked records in all sixteen non-PHP-Wasm profiles on both source routes; PHP-Wasm callback positions have their own hosted archive; retained or asynchronous callbacks and owned checked records remain separate.

The Node R2 fixture additionally checks a host-produced `Fin 3` reply ([reviewed Fin receipt](../evidence/reviewed-callback-fin-20261008/npm-r2.json)). The reviewed Fin archive does not establish reviewed-browser execution, native host-produced replies, `Fin 0` or wider bounds.

[Hosted PHP-Wasm callback acceptance](../evidence/callback-refinements-php-wasm-promotion-20261023.md) covers the fixture's synchronous `Fin`, `Interval` and `Weighted` callback arguments and replies and returned-closure inputs and results. Each ordinary-source and reviewed-IR route runs in twelve Node/Chromium arrangements. The Fin corpus executes 23 checks per arrangement and the checked-record corpus executes 30.
